name: ToggleButton

examples.title: Controlled
Colors
examples.code:
<Buttons>
  <ToggleButton defaultPressed>Link</ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton color="primary" defaultPressed>
    Primary
  </ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton color="info" defaultPressed>
    Info
  </ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton color="success" defaultPressed>
    Success
  </ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton color="danger" defaultPressed>
    Danger
  </ToggleButton>
</Buttons>

examples.code:
<Buttons>
  <ToggleButton size="small">Small</ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton defaultPressed>Normal</ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton size="medium" isRounded>
    Medium
  </ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton size="large" isRounded defaultPressed>

examples.title: Icon-Only
A Set of Toggles
examples.code:
<Buttons hasAddons role="group" aria-label="Text style">
  <ToggleButton aria-label="Bold" defaultPressed>
    <Icon name="bold" />
  </ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton aria-label="Italic">
    <Icon name="italic" />
  </ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton aria-label="Underline">
    <Icon name="underline" />
  </ToggleButton>
</Buttons>

examples.title: Picking One of Several
examples.code:
<Radios label="View" name="view" defaultValue="list">
  <Radio value="list"> List </Radio>
  <Radio value="grid"> Grid </Radio>
</Radios>

examples.title: Inside a Form
Stopping a Toggle
examples.code:
<ToggleButton
  onClick={event => {
    const turningOn =
      event.currentTarget.getAttribute('aria-pressed') === 'false';
    if (turningOn && !window.confirm('Anyone with the link will see it.')) {
      event.preventDefault();
    }
  }}
>
  Public
</ToggleButton>

examples.title: Loading
Disabled
examples.code:
<Buttons>
  <ToggleButton isDisabled>Show archived</ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton isDisabled defaultPressed>
    Show archived
  </ToggleButton>
</Buttons>

accessibility:
`ToggleButton` follows the toggle button in the
[APG button pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/):

- **Role and state:** it's a native `<button>` with `aria-pressed` set to `"true"` or `"false"`
  from the first render, server markup included, so it's announced as a toggle button, pressed or
  not pressed. It's never `"mixed"`.
- **Keyboard:** <kbd>Enter</kbd> and <kbd>Space</kbd> toggle it, as on any button, and focus stays
  on it.
- **Loading:** while `isLoading` is set, it carries `aria-busy="true"`, and keys hold it still the
  same as the pointer does. It keeps focus, since it isn't disabled.
- **The label stays put:** APG says "it is critical the label on a toggle does not change when its
  state changes." Mute stays "Mute". An icon can change, but the `aria-label` doesn't. A label that
  changes, "Play" and then "Pause", belongs on a plain `Button` with no `aria-pressed`. Nothing can
  check this at runtime, so it's yours to keep.
- **Icon-only toggles** need an `aria-label`, as on `Button`.
- **On is easy to see:** the default `link` fill turns a light button solid blue, and a dark one
  bright in dark mode, so it's a change in lightness and not only in hue. `color` leaves out the
  fills that wouldn't be: `white`, `light`, `dark` and `black` each match a plain button's
  lightness in one theme or the other. That's also why the pressed look isn't
  `Button`'s `isActive` shade:
  [WCAG's own example](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html) of a
  button marked only by a darker shade of its color "would not pass Use of color".
- **A set has a name:** give the `Buttons` around a set of toggles `role="group"` and an
  `aria-label`.
- **One choice from several** is a radio group, not a set of toggles, so it's `Radios`.
summary: The `ToggleButton` component renders a button that stays pressed until it's pressed again, and says whether it's on through `aria-pressed`. It's always a `<button type="button">`, so it never submits a form and carries no form value: a setting saved with a form is a `Checkbox` or a `Switch`. A set of toggles that each turn on and off on their own goes in `Buttons hasAddons` with `role="group"` and an `aria-label`. A set where only one can be on is a radio group rather than a row of these: use `Radios`.

props.name: pressed
props.description: Whether it's pressed, when you hold the state. Setting it makes the toggle controlled: a click only calls `onPressedChange`, and nothing changes until you pass the new value. Pick this or `defaultPressed` for the button's lifetime.

props.name: defaultPressed
props.description: Whether it starts pressed, when it holds its own state.

props.name: onPressedChange
props.description: Called with the new state each time it's toggled, by a click, Enter or Space, whether or not `pressed` is set. An `onClick` that calls `preventDefault()` stops the toggle, and this doesn't fire.

props.name: color
props.description: The fill while it's pressed. Not pressed, it's a plain button, so the fill is the difference people see. `white`, `light`, `dark` and `black` aren't offered, since in one theme or the other each fills about as light or dark as a plain button already is. Of the rest, a pale one such as `warning` changes less than the default `link`.

props.name: children
props.description: The label, which stays the same in both states: a screen reader announces whether it's pressed, so "Mute" stays "Mute". An icon can swap, but an icon-only toggle needs an `aria-label` that doesn't. A label that changes ("Play", then "Pause") belongs on a plain `Button`.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows Bulma's spinner in place of the label and holds the toggle where it is: a click, Enter or Space does nothing, so neither `onClick` nor `onPressedChange` fires, until it's cleared. Set it while a change is saving. The button carries `aria-busy="true"` meanwhile and stays focusable, so focus isn't lost mid-save. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the spinner stops and stays drawn (with bestax's CSS loaded).

props.name: isFullWidth
props.deprecationNote: Use `isFullwidth` instead — `isFullwidth` wins if both are set.
